text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Flagging quarterly sales figures issued yesterday by David Jones Ltd and Coles Myer Ltd, coupled with another fall in the ANZ Bank's measure of job vacancies - which counts positions advertised in metropolitan newspapers - have increased pressure for a cut in official interest rates, to be considered by the Reserve Bank board today. Page 1.

Queensland Sugar Corporation chief executive David Rutledge said yesterday most of Queensland's 1996-97 crop had been sold and priced and most of it would probably be sold in the Asian market, which continues to grow faster than the world average. However, Rutledge indicated the world market was expected to remain in surplus in the short-medium term, placing pressure on sugar prices. Page 2.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday singled out fringe benefits tax as one of the most important items in the Small Business Deregulation task force's report on ways of cutting small business red tape. Howard said the Government would not abolish the tax, but it would look at changes to make it less burdensome. Page 3.

Coles Myer Ltd has recorded one of the weakest sales growth numbers since the last recession, with a 5.6 per cent increase in first quarter sales to A$4,445 million in the 13 weeks to October 27. The Kmart division suffered a 5.3 per cent decline in sales, while the supermarkets and liquor division and the Target chain all recorded creditable sales increases. Page 17.

Despite three of its four divisions returning a healthy rise in earnings, diversified manufacturer Email Ltd said yesterday a 10.4 per cent fall in net profit, coupled with an uncertain economic outlook had led the group to cut its dividend for the first half of the 1997 financial year. Page 19.

In a speech at Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd annual general meeting yesterday, chairman Brian Powers offered shareholders little insight into the company's long-term strategy for pay-TV, saying only that it would keep its choices open and wants the option of becoming a key player in the industry. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The BT-MCI telecommunications merger has increased speculation about the future of MCI's A$2.53 billion deal with The News Corporation Ltd, with MCI chairman Bert Roberts saying on the weekend that MCI would not be increasing its investment as had originally been planned. Page 25.

In a move which will see Westpac Banking Corp cancel almost five per cent of its issued share capital, the bank announced a surprise A$600 million share buyback yesterday, renewing speculation the bank is shaping up as a major takeover target following the Wallis inquiry and triggering a surge of buying in Westpac shares. Page 25.

In a bid to win the battle against banks for retail customers, two of Australia's big life insurance offices, GIO Australia and the AMP Society's Priority One, will between them launch two home loans and two lending products with interest rates which will undercut many of the banks. Page 27.

To make way for the proposed A$10 billion co-development of the next phase of the North West Shelf gas project, Chevron Asiatic Ltd expects to soon resolve the restructuring of the ownership of the Chrysaor gas discovery. Chevron hopes to bring Chrysaor ownership into line with that of the Gorgon field, to encourage a co-development with the Shelf project's partners. Page 27.

Optus Vision has appointed two advertising salespeople to start selling ads for its 23-channel pay TV service, in preparation for restrictions on pay TV advertising being lifted in July next year. It is estimated that pay TV could cut about 10 per cent of the free-to-air channels' advertising revenue. Page 27.

Although Coles Myer Ltd yesterday reported a 5.6 per cent increase in sales for the 13 weeks to October 27, the retailer conceded the pace of growth had slowed from previous quarters. Its rival, David Jones Ltd, announced a 2.9 per cent fall in revenue for the first quarter, from A$319.8 million to A$310.5 million. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following disappointing results for the first quarter of their 1997 year, retail giants Coles Myer and David Jones are not confident Christmas trade will be enough to lift consumer trading from the doldrums. David Jones said yesterday its first-quarter sales fell 2.9 per cent to A$310.5 million and Coles Myer said sales for the 13 weeks to October 27 were up 5.6 per cent from the same time last year, but that the growth was weaker than it had achieved recently. Page 25.

At Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting annual general meeting yesterday, executive chairman Brian Powers said the group expects to overcome the weak economy and soft advertising market to lift operating profits in television and magazines this financial year. Page 25.

In a move that signals it has wound down its aggressive acquisition program for the time being and that comes shortly after an on-market buyback of 95 million shares, Westpac Banking Corp has announced it will spend at least A$600 million to buyback 85 million, or five per cent, of its ordinary shares. Page 25.

Email directors yesterday posted a 10 per cent fall in net profit to A$23.8 million for the half-year to September 30 and announced they had decided to reduce the half-year dividend to eight cents per share, compared with 11.5 cents last year. The result has raised speculation that the appliance group will cut its full-year dividend for the second successive year. Page 27.

GIO Insurance Ltd reported a marginal increase in net profit for the year to June 30 yesterday, up one per cent to A$142.2 million. Managing director Bill Jocelyn said the insurer hopes better-performing investment markets and no natural disasters will help profits more than match last year's return. Page 27.
THE AGE

As part of a continuing program of capital management by Westpac, managing director Robert Joss yesterday announced a second share buyback program of 85 million shares over six months. The move will cost Westpac about A$600 million and follows an earlier share buyback between March and July. Page C1.

Coles Myer Ltd's supermarkets and liquor division helped the retailer post a sales increase of 5.6 per cent to A$4.45 billion yesterday, but its Myer Grace Bros, Kmart and Katies stores continued to struggle. David Jones Ltd, also exposed to the
poorly prforming apparel industry, posted a 2.9 per cent drop in sales. Page C1.

In a speech in Brisbane last night, secretary of the Treasury, Ted Evans, called on all savers and investors to take more responsibility for the outcomes of their investment decisions and criticised the quality of the submissions to the Wallis inquiry, climing some parts of the industry had been too timid and failed to look to the future. Page C1.

Despite reporting a 10 per cent fall in net profit to A$23.8 million for the six months to 30 September, appliance maker Email Ltd's shares rose seven cents yesterday to finish at A$3.62. Directors said the first-half dividend would be reduced to eight cents a share, compared with 11.5 cents last year. Page C3.

BT Funds Management said yesterday it would raise A$124 million through a three-for-10 renouncable rights issue for the Grosvenor Trust to buy six adjoining properties in Sydney's central business district, on Macquarie, Hunter and Phillip
Streets. PageC3.

Despite a restructuring racking up abnormal costs of A$6.9 million, Australia's biggest friendly society, IOOF, reported a A$4.1 million profit yesterday after a A$4.1 million loss last year. IOOF has more than 300,000 members and about A$3 billion in fuds under management. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
